problem:
A biologist has recorded data on a pine tree's age (in years) and height (in feet). This data is shown below. 

| Age $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Height $(y)$ | $1.2$ | $2.5$ | $3.6$ | $4.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the tree's height after $8$ years, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}15 & -5 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}11.8 \\ 35\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*

feedback.problem:
The relationship between the advertising budget and sales (both in millions of dollars) of a company per year over several years is shown in the following table. 

| Advertising $(x)$ | **$2$** | **$2.5$** | **$3$** | **$3.5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sales $(y)$ | $10$ | $12$ | $16$ | $20$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the total sales when the annual advertising budget is equal to $$5$ million, assuming the trend continues? 

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}31.5 & -11 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}58 \\ 168\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2.5 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 3.5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 12 \\ 16 \\ 20\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

 

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}31.5 & -11 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}58 \\ 168\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4.2 \\ 6.8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=-4.2+6.8x.$ 

Finally, to predict the value of the sales when the advertising budget is equal to $$5$ million, we substitute $x=5$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4.2+6.8(5) \\  & =29.8\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the total sales when the advertising budget equals $$5$ million will be $$29.8$ million. 

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=5$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.
